output.answer: IBM does not have a single, company-wide Chief Technology Officer today: its official Senior Leadership page (checked as of 2026-11-11) lists Chairman, President and CEO Arvind Krishna and his direct reports with no 'Chief Technology Officer' among them. Instead, CTO titles at IBM are unit- and region-level roles — e.g., Jason McGee is IBM Fellow and CTO of IBM Cloud, Dr. Amith Singhee is CTO for IBM India and South Asia, Shanker V Selvadurai is VP & CTO of IBM Technology for Asia Pacific, Harish Bharti was elevated to CTO Asia Pacific for IBM Consulting in September 2026, and Jessica Rockwood was appointed CTO of IBM Canada in August 2026. So any answer naming 'IBM's CTO' refers to a specific unit or region, not a corporate-wide officer.
caveats: IBM's own senior-leadership page confirms no company-wide CTO exists, so a source naming a single 'IBM CTO' is almost certainly referring to a unit- or region-level CTO (IBM Cloud, IBM India/South Asia, IBM Technology APAC, IBM Consulting APAC, IBM Canada, etc.).

Some third-party and social profiles (e.g., older LinkedIn headlines such as 'CTO at IBM') can be stale or refer to long-standing unit-level roles; the only current corporate-level fact verifiable from IBM's official page is that no CTO is listed.
Unit-level CTO roles change frequently — e.g., Harish Bharti's appointment was announced in September 2026 and Jessica Rockwood's in August 2026 — so any named unit CTO could change.
